Identifier allocation and sequence reuse behavior for the semaphore identifier table
Reference counting and deferred reclamation details for array and undo objects

findings.text: Kernel helper ksys_semget accepts a key plus a count plus flags and the semget system call forwards to it, so both names expose the same acquisition contract.

Set acquisition validates the requested count against a negative lower bound and a namespace maximum, packages key and flags and count into a parameter object, and delegates to generic IPC dispatch with creation plus association plus size-compatibility callbacks.
Creation requires a nonzero count and requires that in-use total plus request stay within the namespace ceiling; per-set reuse requires the requested count to stay within the stored element count.

Sizing for a new set uses a zeroed flexible object with an overflow guard derived from integer maximum and element size, and observable initial state has empty per-element and global wait structures, cleared complex tracking with a hysteresis seed, recorded element count and creation time, caller key preserved, and mode confined to ordinary access permissions.

Set container holds a permission subobject and element count and creation time and complex-waiter count and a global-lock mode indicator plus global alteration and constant wait lists plus an identity list for undo associations plus element storage.
Each element holds a numeric value and a last-actor identifier and a last-operation timestamp plus dedicated alteration and constant wait lists and dedicated synchronization.

Queued request holds an operation vector and operation count and undo context and originator identifier and sleeper reference and remembered blocking operation and completion status plus queue linkage and a repeated-index indicator.

A multi-element attempt is all-or-nothing over values and undo adjustments with zero-test and negativity and upper-bound checks plus undo-range checks; outcomes are full success or deferral with remembered blocking element or immediate failure for nonblocking callers or range failure with compensation of partial effects.

Requests without repeated indexes follow validate-then-commit without partial writes, while requests with repeated indexes follow incremental update with backward compensation and deferred actor recording.

Progress handling separates observing waiters from altering waiters, prefers per-element queues when affected indexes are known and otherwise scans broadly, re-evaluates altering waiters in order with restart when global alteration work exists or the completed waiter was complex, and refreshes modification time when any waiter completes.
Queue removal detaches linkage and decrements the complex counter exactly when the request spans more than one element.

Waiter census for one index counts per-element queue membership directly and filters global queues by blocked index and operation kind, distinguishing zero-wait from decrement-wait, with a one-time notice about historical counting differences.

After teardown starts no undo association stays linked and no waiter stays queued in global or per-element lists; per-element actor records are cleared, the identifier is detached, namespace usage is reduced by the element count, and reclamation is deferred after batched wakeups with a removed-set error delivered to every waiter.

Lookup runs under read-side critical section with checked and unchecked variants; mutation takes the array lock and revalidates liveness under that lock; teardown asserts the object lock; large bulk paths take a reference, release locks for allocation or user copy, then reacquire with reference drop and liveness recheck.

Object destruction ordering detaches identifiers and releases the array lock and exits the read-side critical section before performing batched wakeups, and identifier removal plus reference release are paired with deferred freeing.

Status queries distinguish positional lookup from validated lookup; read permission is required except for the audit-only variant, a security check always applies, liveness is rechecked under lock, and the reported operation time is the maximum over elements while change time and element count come from the set header.
User status transfer supports a native 64-bit form and an older form with permission conversion plus operation and change times plus element count, and rejects unknown versions.

Information query reports namespace tunables for set count and total elements and per-set length and per-call operation count together with value ceiling and informational constants, reports live usage under a read guard on the identifier table, and returns highest index or zero when empty.

Single-value assignment is allowed only for values between zero and the global ceiling with write access and security approval and liveness under lock; visible effects are cleared undo adjustments for that index, updated value and actor and change time, and waiter re-evaluation.

Bulk read requires read access and bulk write requires write access; incoming bulk values are range-checked before commit, commit assigns all values and actors and clears all undo adjustments and updates change time with waiter re-evaluation, using a stack buffer for small sets and dynamic allocation for large sets.

Single-index queries for value and actor and waiter counts validate the index, recheck liveness under lock, harden the index against speculation, and then report the stored value or numeric actor or computed census.
Caller-controlled indexes are clamped with speculation hardening before element access in validation paths and commit paths and control paths.
Waiter completion publishes status with release ordering before safely queuing a held sleeper reference for batched wakeup outside locks, avoiding wakeup while holding array state.
Range contracts use a global per-element value ceiling and a symmetric undo magnitude bound plus informational sizing constants and a fast-path bulk threshold.
Control surface uses bulk read and bulk write and per-index value and actor and waiter-count operations plus single-value assignment plus stat and info queries plus native and old version selectors.
Behavior modifiers use an undo flag and a nonblocking flag, and access uses read and write and full permission masks for status versus mutation.
